summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Research design and 21 source leads for Nepal's digital infrastructure and cybersecurity baseline. Q1 (broadband penetration, speeds, prices): NTA MIS/annual report (subscription-based, Nepali-calendar months), ITU DataHub/WDI (person-based, calendar year), ITU Price Baskets, and crowd-sourced speed data are defined as distinct measures and kept apart. Q2 (international routes and redundancy): design to enumerate each cross-border fibre route, capacity and physical corridor and test single-point-of-failure exposure; NTA and Nepal Telecom disclosures and ITU bandwidth data are the leads. Q3 (laws): status register for the Electronic Transactions Act, Individual Privacy Act, National Cyber Security Policy, any IT/cyber bill, NTA IT Policy and NRB guidelines, each to be confirmed from primary text. Most NTA, MoCIT and Law Commission URLs are home pages from general knowledge (unverified). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending.

findings.claim: Definitions for Q1: (a) NTA 'internet/broadband penetration' is subscriptions per 100 population and counts SIMs/data packs, so it can exceed individual use; (b) ITU/WDI 'individuals using the internet' is a person-based survey/estimate; (c) speeds from crowd-sourced tests (Ookla) are not representative samples. These are reported side by side, never averaged. NTA months follow the Nepali calendar; ITU/WDI are calendar years.

Route-redundancy design for Q2: enumerate each international terrestrial fibre route (border crossing point, operator, partner-country carrier, lit capacity), then test single-point-of-failure exposure: share of international bandwidth by country (India vs China) and by physical corridor, and whether diverse paths survive a single landslide/earthquake corridor loss. Physical-hazard overlay coordinated with 24D and 16B.

Legal-framework design for Q3: status categories = in force (Act/Regulation with commencement date), policy only (Cabinet-approved policy, not law), draft bill, absent. Primary text from the Law Commission or issuing ministry is required for 'in force'; news is a locator only.
Q1: fixed broadband subscriptions (total and FTTH) and mobile broadband subscriptions, by operator, latest month and FY time series.

challenges.text: Add bandwidth/speed unit codes (Mbit/s, Gbit/s) to units.py (also requested by 24B); add catalog ids for mocit_nepal and for industry registries (PeeringDB, Ookla) or confirm they fall under 'academic'. Allocate a network run to fetch 08B-L01, L02, L14, L15, L16.
08B's legal_framework_status register overlaps your defensive-posture benchmarks; propose 08B holds statute status and dates, 24D holds benchmark scoring, to avoid duplicate observations.
Support treating international connectivity dependence on India-routed transit as an exposure entry, pending route data from 08B-L02/L11.
Red-team: any strategy premised on data-centre or digital-service exports should be checked against route redundancy and the absence (unverified) of data-centre regulation.

uncertainty: High. No values retrieved. Definitions of penetration differ materially across NTA and ITU; speed data are non-representative; route and capacity data may be commercially confidential and unavailable; legal status may have changed since the last located document.

connectivity_baseline.method: NTA administrative subscriptions, ITU person-based use and crowd-sourced speeds are kept as separate observations with their definitions; NTA Nepali-month data are not mixed with calendar-year ITU data without conversion.

questions: Which cross-border fibre links (India border points; China via the northern corridor) are lit, by which operators, with what capacity?
What share of international bandwidth depends on India-routed transit?
Do the routes share physical corridors exposed to the same landslide/earthquake hazards?
Is there domestic IXP and caching that keeps domestic traffic local during an international outage?
